title: Observability Lens — Weekly Brief (tracing, dashboards, cost telemetry)
content:
Summary:

This brief captures the Observability team’s work this week focused on three areas: tracing sampling experiments, a small dashboard refresh for the latency/cost view, and initial telemetry knobs for prefix/KV cache visibility. It’s an explicit working note: lots of open questions, experimental results, and tasks to hand off to SRE and platform teams.

Highlights:
- Sampling experiment v2 completed on 8/02 across two customer-facing services (inbox and routing-service). Early signal: tail latency traces preserved for ~95% of P99 events while reducing total trace volume by ~28%.
- Latency vs token-cost dashboard (temp view) shipped to staging; first round of feedback from Solutions Eng shows it surfaces the right tradeoffs for bursty workflows.
- Prototype metric exporter for KV cache hit/miss (per-model, per-route) merged to the feature branch — PR 421. Needs production hardening.

Meeting notes (Standup & Working Sync 2026-08-04, 11:00–12:00 PST):
Attendees: Maya, Jon, Priya, Lucas, Anika, SRE rep: Darren.
- Maya: sampling results summary, suggested moving canary to 10% of traffic for 24 hrs before wider rollout.
- Jon: dashboard filters still slow for multi-tenant queries; traced down to a high-cardinality tag (model_variant). Proposal: add sampled cardinality bucketization in the query pipeline.
- Priya: KV cache exporter working in dev, but observed double-counting in two test harnesses — likely race in metric aggregation.
- Lucas: traced an alert storm when trace ingestion backpressure hit; recommended immediate rate-limit fallback to a compact trace format (drop spans with zero-metrics).
- Darren (SRE): agreed to run a capacity exercise next Wed, and requested that tracing pipeline expose current ingestion headroom metric (INGEST_HEADROOM).

Incident review (small brief):
- 2026-08-01 02:42 UTC: short-lived ingestion spike caused retention worker backlog and delayed dashboards for ~18 minutes. Root cause: noisy synthetic test deployment triggered repeated long traces. Postmortem in progress (linked in artifacts). Immediate mitigation: temporary throttle for test-namespaces and a filter to drop synthetic-only spans.

Tracing experiments (details & notes):
- Sampling v2 parameters: 0.6 base rate for error traces + adaptive tail-preserve policy (priority to traces where service latency > 3x baseline).
- Results (canary 1% → global simulated): preserved 96% of error traces, 95% of P99 traces, reduced total spans ~28%.
- Outstanding question: does adaptive tail-preserve bias against low-traffic customers? We saw slight under-capture for customers with <50 RPS. Action: set explicit per-tenant min-capture override (Ticket OBS-420).
- Next: expand canary to 10% traffic for inbox and routing-service for 24 hours (owner: Maya, due: 2026-08-06).

Dashboards & Queries (what changed):
- New latency-vs-cost dashboard (staging): combined charts show tokens/sec, token-cost-per-request, average latency, and trace-sampled P95/P99. UX notes: default time window 30m, user can toggle model_variant bucketization.
- Performance work: large multi-tenant queries degrade when model_variant cardinality > 1k. Interim fix: sample model_variant values for visualization (Jon). Longer-term: pre-aggregate by shard (platform-engineering ticket).
- Action: add a ‘cost-normalized-latency’ derived metric to help product make placement decisions (owner: Priya, prototype due 2026-08-12).

Cost telemetry & unit economics:
- Initial analysis: traces are ~12% of our observability ingestion egress costs for heavy customers; spans volume correlates strongly with SDK verbosity and KV cache misses.
- Hypothesis: targeted sampling + KV cache telemetry will reduce per-customer trace egress by 20–30% without sacrificing debugging signal.
- Quick wins identified: (1) SDK default verbosity reduction for non-dev envs, (2) enable prefix cache heatmap and encourge caching on frequent prompt patterns.

Runbook & Operational items:
- Runbook update required: add step to flip canary sampling rates and emergency rollback (file: runbooks/tracing-rate-adjust.md — cf. linked artifacts).
- Add INGEST_HEADROOM to alerting (SLO owner: Darren). Alert threshold: headroom < 15% for >5m => paging.
- Create compact-span-format fallback (Lucas to draft design, due 2026-08-09).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we make per-tenant min-capture an explicit customer opt-in or opt-out? Legal/policy might care for regulated customers (Anika to coordinate with Security & Compliance).
- Do we allow the dashboard to expose raw model_variant values to all internal users? Risk: high cardinality leak of customer model names. Proposal: mask high-cardinality variants beyond 100 examples and expose hashed token for internals-only lookups.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Maya: expand sampling canary to 10% for inbox & routing-service, monitor for 24h (due 2026-08-06).
- Jon: implement sampled cardinality bucketization on visualization pipeline (due 2026-08-11).
- Priya: prototype cost-normalized-latency metric + add to staging dashboard (due 2026-08-12).
- Lucas: draft compact-span-format fallback and ingestion behavior (due 2026-08-09).
- Anika: coordinate with Security & Compliance on per-tenant min-capture policy (due 2026-08-13).
- Darren (SRE): run capacity exercise for trace ingestion and expose INGEST_HEADROOM metric (scheduled 2026-08-12).

Notes to self / working thoughts (informal):
- Need to keep telemetry lightweight; dashboards are great but if they drive 10x query costs they become a regression. Keep derived metrics and pre-aggregation as defaults.
- Watch out for double-counting — seen in the KV exporter where both exporter and ingestion agent increment the same counter. Could add a process-id label to prevent it.
- Consider a small UI for internal ops to temporarily increase sampling for a tenant for debugging (time-bound increases only). Could be a toggle on the per-tenant page in Console.

Links & references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/421 (KV cache exporter)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/obs/runbooks/prefix-caching
- Jira: OBS-412 (sampling v2), OBS-420 (per-tenant min-capture), OBS-428 (dashboard perf), OBS-435 (compact-span-format)

Next week plan (short):
- Harden KV exporter and ship to canary infra (Priya + Lucas).
- Complete dashboard perf patch and measure query latency improvements (Jon).
- Run the ingestion capacity exercise with SRE and iterate on fallback thresholds (Maya + Darren).
- Draft user-facing guidance for Solutions Eng on interpreting cost-normalized-latency.

If you have questions or want a deeper dive into sampling numbers, ping me in slack:#observability or add notes here — I’ll append results post-canary.

— Maya
